description: Original polished HD-2D game pixel-art single isolated static sprite. Fixed camera looks down 35 degrees from above, orthographic-like three-quarter volume, not a flat side elevation. Clear readable silhouette, deliberately placed crisp pixel clusters, natural low-saturation midtone colors, detailed but not noisy, soft colored contour accents rather than heavy black outlines. Neutral broad diffuse daytime material color for later real-time lighting: no night tint, no glow, no colored rim light, no directional cast shadow, no ground, no platform, no scenery, no text, no checkerboard. Entire subject visible with a few transparent margin pixels, transparent RGBA background. One enormous densely leafed mature summer OAK TREE, a whole single tree. IMPORTANT: abundant thick leafy canopy is the main subject: a large continuous broad dome of overlapping rounded uneven foliage masses covers the entire upper TWO THIRDS, 90 percent of canvas width, with only tiny deep openings. The canopy is rich, lush and thick, not sparse, not disconnected little leaf balls. Upper branches are hidden almost entirely inside leaves. Only one short massive mossy bark trunk with a wide fork is visible in the bottom THIRD, with heavy flared woody roots. A dignified old 6-meter temperate oak with a huge shady crown, wild asymmetrical edge, layered olive and muted grey-green leaves with subtle warmer leaf patches, very convincing volumetric pixel-cluster shading. Stout grey-brown deeply fissured bark and green lichen. No grass, no ground plane, no props. Show the top of the dense canopy due to 35-degree elevated camera. No exposed bare branches outside the leafy crown.
